title: ARIA live-region stabilization and focus resilience sweep for dense controls
creator: Ava Park
description: Sweep to harden ARIA live regions, keyboard focus behavior, and contrast token edge cases across compact/dense variants of buttons, tables, and chart widgets. Scope covers visual and semantic focus (tab order, roving tabindex), screen-reader announcements for live filters and inline edits, and contrast ramps for compact tokens. Deliverables: updated token mapping, component change notes, VPAT evidence pack, and a lightweight QA harness for cross-screenreader smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: All dense button/table/chart variants have deterministic focus order and documented tab sequences
Live-region announcements for incremental updates (filters, streaming charts, inline edits) do not duplicate messages and are correctly labeled in VoiceOver and NVDA
Contrast token adjustments include test cases for 3:1 and 4.5:1 scenarios and are recorded in the design token changelog
VPAT appendix includes before/after examples and screenreader log snippets for reviewers
Design tokens and CSS variables updated with migration notes and a rollout plan for runtime-1.18 and ds-2026.03
tasks: Run component audit across compact density variants and record failing scenarios (keyboard, ARIA, contrast)
Add integration tests to accessibility-harness (aria-live smoke cases + keyboard traversal traces)
Propose token adjustments and map visual deltas to a migration guide
Ship design-system PR with updated styles and aria annotations
Coordinate engineering rollouts with ENG (canary + monitoring for regressions)
Assemble VPAT evidence pack and attach to Confluence page for compliance review
decisions: Prefer semantic roles (role=button/region/table) and native elements where possible to reduce custom ARIA surface
Use single live-region per widget with polite policy and concise summarization to avoid screenreader thrash
Implement CSS-only focus ring for compact tokens to avoid layout shifts; add aria-describedby only when necessary
Defer structural rewrites for virtualized tables to a follow-up (ENG-33210) to minimize release risk
notes: We observed NVDA repeating filter changes when both aria-live and aria-atomic were used on nested nodes; consolidated to parent-only announcements
Compact chart tooltip updates should use aria-hidden on purely decorative layers and expose summaries via a single aria-live region
Contrast adjustments focus first on interactive foregrounds (text/icon) before modifying background ramp to keep visual density
